g.aria-label: Justification table for *2.16 ver of Transp For *2.05 cf Syll table.
Note: this is a more compact version of the notation used in the demonstration/proof of Praeclarum Theorema. Cf (as written) text for *2.80 and PT/*3.47

Note: "*2.53.31" is identical to "*2.53∧*2.31". I am taking advantage of the similarity in meaning between modern and dot notations for notational concision. E.g. if it was typed horizontally, the citation for *2.75 would be: "[*2.74 ~q/q]∧*2.53.31" (in a box, of course).

Note: It's pointed out in the book that "This is called the 'prinicple of identity' and referred to as 'Id'. It is not the same as the 'law of identity' ('x is identical with x') but the law of identity is inferred from it'. Worth keeping in mind.

Note from the book: "The proofs of *2.37.38 are exactly analogous to that of *2.36"
Note from me: Due to the above note in the book, I am treating this as a sort of lateral citation and thus will include the full graph of *2.36 for completeness.

Note from the book: "This definition serves only for the avoidance of brackets."
Note from me: Interestingly, although I render 'p∨q∨r' the way I do in order to adhere faithfully to the text as written, it also saves space in a spatialized graph to do so, not just in text.
It's included here because I consider it 'indirectly' cited when it is used, as its use is missing context when not included. Hence, e.g., *2.74 in my opinion can be considered an 'indirect citation' of *2.33.

path.aria-label: Note by me: In the book the attached note refers to both *3.27 and *3.26 as being called the principle of simplification much like *2.02. Also, I normally leave out the QEDs as they don't really do much ohter than restate the proof and theroem to be proved in shorthand but, here, it's worth pointing out that they directly and explicitly cite *3.01 as part of the QED. Other instances of *3.01 being inferred, explicitly or otherwise, will be omitted from the graph/proof for reasons of concision and clarity, as will be references to *1.01, if they are not part of the main body of a proof/demonstration. Cf the text of *2.33 for more on that reasoning.
*3.03 (as written): "Given two asserted elementary propositional functions '⊢.ⲫp' and '⊢.ψp' whose arguments are elementary propositions, we have ⊢.ⲫp.ψp."
Note by me: Cf *3.26 text for why *1.11/the QED aren't included in the graph.
*1.71 (as written) "If p and q are elementary propositions, p∨q is an elementary proposition."
*1.72 (as written) "If ⲫp and ψp are elementary propositional functions which take elementary propositions as arguments, ⲫp∨ψp is an elementary propositional function."
*1.10 (as written) "Anything implied by a true elementary proposition is true."
*1.11 (as written) "When ⲫx can be asserted, where x is a real variable, and ⲫx⊃ψx can be asserted, where x is a real variable, then can be asserted, where x is a real variable."
*1.70 (as written) "If p is an elementary proposition, ~p is an elementary proposition."
